To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acute hypertension provokes acute redistribution of DCT NCC from APL to SCV and that this redistribution is secondary to the decrease of ANG II that occurs during hypertension.

acute increases in blood pressure cause internalization of Ncc from apical plasma membranes to subapical vesicles, which is driven by a fall in angiotensin II and may contribute to pressure-induced diuresis.
acute hypertension provokes acute redistribution of distal tubular NCC to subapical vesicles and that this redistribution contributes to the pressure diuresis response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of sodium reabsorption by the distal convoluted tube (DCT) and the role of this regulation in the control of arterial pressure and volume homeostasis.
the regulation of renal salt transporters, and in particular, with the regulation of the distal tubule sodium chloride cotransporter (NaCl cotransporter, NCC).
the mechanisms of blood pressure regulation, particularly the regulation of blood volume and the role of renal tubule function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acute hypertension provokes acute redistribution of DCT Na(+)-Cl (-) cotransporter from plasma membrane to subapical endosomes, which contributes to the acute natriuresis.

the acute fall of ANG II that occurs during acute hypertension is a key factor for the acute redistribution of NCC to subapical compartments, and that this process is important in the acute natriuretic response.
acute hypertension induces acute trafficking of distally located NCC into SCVs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acute hypertension causes a decrease in apical membrane NCC, which contributes to the natriuresis and that this is mediated in part by the fall in plasma ANG II.
acute hypertension provokes acute redistribution of DCT NCC to the subapical vesicles, which is driven, at least in some part, by the fall in angiotensin II.
acute hypertension provokes acute redistribution of distal tubular NCC to subapical vesicles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NCC trafficking may participate in the pressure natriuresi-diuresis response by decreasing APM and increasing SCV pool size of NCC.
the acute fall in angiotensin II that accompanies acute increases in blood pressure may contribute to the pressure natriuresi by provoking internalization of Ncc in the distal tubule.
NCC trafficking in response to acute hypertension may contribute to the natriuretic response.
